description: Hello Sugar is a beauty and wellness franchise specializing in full body waxing, sugaring, and laser hair removal, founded in 2015 and franchising since September 2021 through Hello Sugar Franchise, LLC of Mesa, Arizona. The system offers two models: Flagship salons (initial investment $266,042-$736,250) and Suite locations ($90,984-$127,914), with a $50,000 franchise fee, 6% royalty, and limited protected territories. The 2025 FDD reports 108 outlets open at the end of 2024 (87 franchised suites, 3 company suites, 6 franchised flagships, 12 company flagships), up from 75 a year earlier; trade press in 2026 reports 200+ locations open and developing after a 20-salon acquisition. The franchisor discloses no litigation or bankruptcy, offers no financing, and operates an affiliate ecosystem covering advertising, supplies, virtual reception, and franchisee coaching.
territory: Limited protected territory (not exclusive); minimum territory is the lesser of 60,000 people or a 2-mile radius around the approved location. Franchisor will not open another outlet in the Territory during the term if the franchisee is not in default; alternative distribution channels are reserved. (FDD Item 12, printed p51)

financingOffered.value: No — franchisor offers no direct or indirect financing and guarantees no note, lease, or obligation

initialTrainingProgram.value: Initial Management Training Program + Initial Esthetician Training Program, delivered virtually and at your location

additionalTrainingHqRate.value: $50 per trainer per hour at headquarters

annualConvention.value: mandatory annual business meeting/convention; franchisee pays own travel/lodging/meals/wages

socialMediaProgram.value: optional Social Media Marketing Program via Hello Sugar Media; prepay by 10th each month; franchisor may require it if minimums not met

brandFundPurpose.value: advertising, marketing, PR, market research, website development for the System as a whole

generalManagerAllowed.value: Yes — appointed by franchisee, acceptable to franchisor, must complete training

productsToSell.value: must offer and sell all System products and services, including full body waxing and sugaring

competingBusinessProhibited.value: may not engage in any business competing with the franchised outlet, the franchisor/affiliates, or other franchisees

renewalTerms.value: successor agreements of 5 years each if in good standing; $2,500 renewal fee; 6-9 months written notice

terminationByFranchisee.value: may seek termination upon any grounds available by state law

curePeriodOther.value: 30 days to cure any other default

disputeResolution.value: mediation and/or litigation only in Arizona

juryTrialWaiver.value: jury trial and class action waiver in the Franchise Agreement

unitClosureRate2024.value: ~3.2% — 3 franchised suites ceased operations for other reasons in 2024 against ~93 franchised outlets; 0 terminations and 0 non-renewals
unitClosureRate2024.source: Derived from FDD Item 20, printed pp71-74

systemGrowthRate2024.value: ~44% — 75 outlets at end-2023 to 108 at end-2024 (suite-to-flagship conversions affect comparability)
systemGrowthRate2024.source: Derived from FDD Item 20, printed pp73-74

ongoingFeeBurden.value: ~7%+ of gross revenue baseline — 6% royalty (Item 6 p15) + 1% brand fund (Item 6 p18, risable to 2%) + per-location fixed fees (reception, software, tech, BMS: Items 6/11)

investmentToFeeRatio.value: flagship high-end investment $736,250 is ~14.7x the $50,000 franchise fee; suite high-end $127,914 is ~2.6x
investmentToFeeRatio.source: Derived from FDD Items 5/7, printed pp13/25/29

franchisorAlignmentSignal.value: 49.7% of franchisor 2024 revenue came from fees paid by franchisees (Item 8 p37) — franchisor economics depend heavily on franchisee payments
franchisorAlignmentSignal.source: Derived from FDD Item 8, printed p37

maturityStage.value: emerging growth — franchising since 2021-09-15 (Item 1 p8), 108 outlets at end-2024 (Item 20), trade press reports 200+ open and developing after a 20-salon acquisition (observed 2026-09-13)
maturityStage.source: Derived from FDD Items 1/20 + trade press

capitalFit.value: flagship requires $266,042-$736,250 (Item 7 p25); suite $90,984-$127,914 (Item 7 p29); no franchisor financing (Item 10 p33) — buyer needs substantial liquid capital and third-party funding

experienceFit.value: flagship can run with an approved Operating Principal (20%+ equity) and General Manager (Item 15 p54); no personal esthetician license required for flagship owners — suits investor-operators

operationalFit.value: semi-absentee possible for flagships with manager in place; suite model expects the owner to be the licensed esthetician-operator (Item 1 p9; Item 15 p54)

lifestyleFit.value: consumer beauty/wellness business — evenings/weekends retail rhythm; fits buyers comfortable with service-retail operations

riskToleranceFit.value: emerging brand (franchising since 2021) with fast growth and unaudited Item 19 figures — fits buyers comfortable with growth-stage risk, not proven-concept buyers

locationFit.value: limited protected territory (min lesser of 60,000 people or 2-mile radius; Item 12 p51) — fits buyers who accept territory protection without exclusivity

timelineFit.value: site selection, approval, and buildout required (flagship buildout $150k-$450k, Item 7 p26); franchise term 10 years with 5-year renewals (Item 17 p56) — fits buyers with a multi-year horizon

supportFit.value: strong affiliate service ecosystem (media, remote reception, supplies, coaching: Item 1 pp10-11; Item 8 p37) — fits buyers who value done-for-you marketing/ops support over full independence
